newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Sun Resorts Mauritius interim profit up 24.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sun Resorts Mauritius interim profit up 24.5 pct.

text.p: Sun Resorts Mauritius on Wednesday posted a 24.5 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 96.3 million rupees ($4.75 million) for the six months ended 30 June 1996, compared to the corresponding period in 1995.
Company turnover for the half year period went up by 22.4 percent to 650.7 million rupees while profit after tax was 24.7 percent higher at 96.1 million rupees, officials said.
Sun Resorts said improved occupancy rates and opening of a new hotel establishment were behind the growth in financial results.

"The group's hotels in Mauritius achieved an average room occupancy (rate) of 75 percent compared to 71 percent last year notwithstanding the addition of Le Coco Beach," the hotel concern said in a statement.

"The 333-room Le Coco Beach Hotel opened for business on 15th March 1996 and exceeded the board's initial expectation, recording an average room occupancy of 70 percent for the period to 30 June 1996," the statement added.
Sun Resorts Mauritius presently operates two hotels in the Indian Ocean island of Comoros and four hotels in Mauritius. A fifth hotel in Mauritius is expected to open in mid October.

"Forward bookings for our operating hotels are satisfactory but with the opening of Sugar Beach Resort, the group will have increased its number of available rooms in Mauritius by 92 percent since the beginning of the year," the company said.
With these seven hotel establishments, Sun Resorts will have a total capacity of 1,415 rooms.

Sun Resorts Mauritius, a subsidiary of South Africa's Sun International, posted 183.6 million rupees of pre-tax profit for the year ending 31 December 1995, turnover of 1.13 billion rupees and after-tax profit of 186.5 million rupees.
